Two turntables and a rotary mixer in the Enthusiast Place DJ studio under red light (the open-decks setup). Official site photo, the only landscape one there; 4032x3024 original centre-cropped to 16:9 and resized to 1920x1080. Both candidates (photo-1, photo-4) were portrait.
Pool deck with daybeds, umbrellas and Barra Cuda towels, Patong Beach behind. 2560px version of candidate 1; candidate 2 is a CGI render. The site has no party photos, only square flyers.

Crowd at the OASIS floor of OXA Jungle with the OXA arch stage. Full-size version of candidate 1, cropped from the bottom to 16:9 so the 'OXA OASIS' corner badge is gone. Candidate 2 is OXA Beach, a different venue.
Sunset over Ban Tai beach from the Sabaii Bay Beach Club deck (featured image of the venue page). The flyer and the dark Wikimedia beach shot were rejected.

Night crowd at the bar under the 'Retro Mountain' graffiti mural and 'Jungle Club' neon sign. From the gallery in the phangan.events 2026 club article; 1280x960 cropped to 16:9 near the top to keep the signage. Candidates rejected: 1 has a text overlay, 2 is 654px and blurry.

The Haad Rin lighthouse on the rocks at sunset with the Lighthouse Bungalows' red roof; same view as the venue's own flyers. Candidate 1 cropped to 16:9 above its 'Lighthouse Underground Party' text, so it is only 889px wide. No clean original or Commons photo exists; the night shots are narrow portraits and the rest are flyers.

Chill Up at night: neon 'CHILL UP' sign and people on the upper floor, on Ban Tai main road. Official site photo, preferred over candidate 1 (a phone shot of the same building). Candidate 2 is a flyer.

Aerial daytime view of the red-roofed Eden Garden bar on the boulders at Haad Yuan, with a longtail boat; the 'Eden Garden' sign is visible bottom left. Uncropped original of candidate 1 (a drone video still, slightly soft). Candidate 2 is an AI-art flyer.

A real venue photo, not a flyer. It's a straight-on view of the open-sided jungle dance floor at night: the white double-arch DJ booth with the GROOVY TUNES neon sign, a disco ball and lanterns, jungle trees lit purple on both sides, and rugs on a red-lit floor. It's image 8 of 14 in the venue's pinned 'Book your event at Unclave' post (25 Sep 2025); RA lists this account as the venue's website. Unclave's small white logo sits at the bottom-left, and a centred 16:9 crop leaves only its top edge. Cropping slightly above centre (about 40%) hides it fully. The IG CDN link is signed and expires, but the file is saved locally. Rejected: the old dated RA flyer (deleted), the post's first image (an 'AVAILABLE FOR BOOKING' text collage), Groovy Tunes posts (portrait video covers), the empty Groovy Tunes Telegram channel and the empty RA venue photo field.

Party crowd at the main stage under the 'WATERFALL PARTY' neon sign, with blue lasers and jungle leaves. Organiser photo from the venue page, cropped to 16:9 above the organiser logo stamped at the bottom. Both candidates were text-heavy flyers.

Real party photo inside Black Box, from the venue's own YouTube channel: a still of the Dec 19, 2025 night (Gera Dzhio b2b David Chong). It shows the DJ at the decks with candles and red club lights, with dancers on both sides. 16:9 at 1280x720 with no overlays. The small screens showing the DJ names are part of the room. It's a 360-camera frame, so the bottom strip (the floor) is warped red. Rejected: RA and phangan.events have only portrait text flyers. Thai2Night and Instagram og:images are the logo, and Facebook needs a login. HACKED promoter video frames have a big text overlay or are face close-ups, and the Radio Samui stream frames have heavy overlays. Commons only has 2013-2015 Panoramio street shots from before the venue opened.

Hammocks and bamboo daybeds on the sand at Pangea Beach Bar at sunset, sea behind. The venue's own Facebook profile photo (1536x1536), cropped to 16:9. The generic Wikimedia Long Beach candidate was rejected because it doesn't show the bar; the RA venue has no photo.
Candidate 1. The white marble Big Buddha against a blue sky, with visitors on the stairs. Sharp, centred, and the statue survives a 16:9 crop.

Candidate 1. The main ordination hall with its red and gold tiered roofs, under an overcast sky. A centre 16:9 crop cuts only the very tip of the spire. Candidate 2 is portrait and would not survive the crop.
Candidate 1. Soi Rommanee, with pink and pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses and red lanterns. It is not one of the photos listed for areas:phuket-town.

Candidate 1. Thalang Road closed to traffic, with food stalls and crowds between the shophouses. Taken on a Sunday afternoon (3 Jun 2018), so it is daylight, before the lights come on. It is the best of the four shots in the same Commons series. Commons has no evening photo of the market.

Found by Commons search. Sugar palms on the cape headland running down into turquoise sea, on a sunny day. Candidate 1 is generic rocks and sea. Candidate 2 is a palm-silhouette sunset that does not show the cape, and it is also listed for areas:rawai.

The classic view from the viewpoint on a sunny day: Ya Nui Beach, its rock islet, Ko Man island and the road to Promthep. Flickr CC photo found through Openverse; the 2048px original was downscaled to 1280px wide. Candidate 1 is a stormy 2.9:1 panorama, only about 784px wide after a 16:9 crop. Candidate 2 shows only Ko Man. The Commons 'Ya Nui beach.jpg' is already the photo for places:ya-nui-beach, so it was not used.

Surroundings photo, not taken at the rock itself. It is an aerial shot (helicopter, Feb 2014) over the Pa Hin Dam headland, looking down its slope at Nai Harn Beach, The Nai Harn hotel, Nai Harn Lake and the Rawai islands, which is the same view the viewpoint gives. Sharp, natively 16:9, no watermark. I found no freely licensed photo taken at Black Rock: Commons search (English, Thai, Pa Hin Dam/Dum, Laem Mum Nok) and a geosearch with no files within 300 m of 7.7831,98.2975; Openverse; Flickr CC search by text and within 1.2 km (only beach, resort and Windmill photos); Wikidata; no official site exists. The first-pass Commons panorama looks at this headland from the Windmill side, not from the viewpoint. Alternative: phuket101's on-site photos (og:image black-rock-viewpoint-phuket-1.jpg) show the real view but are copyright Phuket 101 / Willy Thuan, a blog with a corner watermark, so not used.

The three bays (Kata Noi, Kata, Karon) from the viewpoint in clear weather, with palm fronds in the foreground. Flickr CC photo; the 2048px original was downscaled to 1280px wide. Candidate 1 is hazy and half banana leaves. Candidate 2 is a dark panorama. Candidate 3 carries a '© Benny Chirvanich' watermark.

Found by Commons search. Kata Beach with turquoise surf and Ko Pu island under a deep blue sky; sharp DSLR shot. Candidate 1 is overcast and mostly sand. Candidate 2 is blocked by hanging vines and is also listed for areas:kata.

Candidate 2. A longtail boat moored in turquoise water off Kata Noi, with Ko Pu and the headland behind; the Panoramio geotag is on Kata Noi beach. I trimmed 4px from each edge to remove a thin picture frame. Candidate 1 is a generic sunset silhouette and is also listed for areas:kata-noi and Mom Tri's. The better beach-level shot (Telgaa, 'Kata noi - panoramio') is already saved as areas-kata-noi.jpg, so I did not use it here.

Candidate 2. The long sandy beach with swimmers, clear water and the wind-turbine headland behind. Candidate 1 is hazy, shows only the rocky north corner and has a prominent bather in the centre. Neither matches the photos used for areas:nai-harn or The Nai Harn hotel.

Elevated view through the trees onto Freedom Beach's curved white sand and turquoise bay with longtail boats. The source is a portrait 1081x1920 original (no larger thumbnail exists); it was cropped to 16:9 on the beach (crop offset y=470), so mark it as modified for CC BY-SA. Both listed candidates were rejected: (2) was flat and dull, the panoramio shot has a Thravel.net watermark.

Classic Patong bay view with longtail boats, the beach and green headland behind. Picked from about 15 Commons Patong photos as brighter and more recognizable than the two listed candidates (the 2nd was overcast).

Bangla Road at night: neon bar signs (Kangaroo Bar etc.) and crowds on the walking street. Listed candidate 1, cropped from 1280x853 to the bottom 1280x720 to cut a small logo in the top-right corner (modified).

The Khao Rang (Rang Hill) viewing deck with visitors, overlooking Phuket Town and the bay. The listed candidate was rejected: hazy, portrait 1200x1600, location not clearly Khao Rang. Found in Commons Category:Rang Hill.

Close-up of a seafood stall at the Rawai Beach fish market: scallops, squid and prawns on ice with yellow Thai price signs. Flickr CC BY 2.0; the photo description confirms the Rawai Beach fish market, Oct/Nov 2019. Commons had no photo of the market itself, only the beach and pier. The listed candidates were the beach only and a portrait of a person.

Night shot of the lit-up NAKA MARKET entrance gate with crowds walking in; the official homepage slider image. It beats the listed og:image (daytime gate, 1200x675), and the Commons candidate is a blurry video still. A small 'Cannabis' neon sign shows at the left of the gate. No free-licensed Naka photo exists on Commons or Openverse.
The Chillva Market central stage with the big CHILLVA MARKET sign at dusk (Sept 2025). Listed candidate; it is the only Chillva photo on Commons and Openverse, and the market has no official website.
Quiet, sunny Nai Yang Beach: casuarina trees, pale sand, turquoise water and a green headland. Listed candidate 1. Candidate 3 (Mai Khao plane banner) is only 1280x320.

Bang Pae Waterfall itself: the cascade falling into a narrow plunge pool between mossy rocks in jungle. Flickr CC BY 2.0, from the 'Bang Pae Waterfall' album, geotagged Thalang, Phuket, taken Nov 2011. All Commons photos (the listed candidates) show only a pond and forest 'near' the falls, not the waterfall.

Five elephants roaming the sanctuary forest below the thatched viewing skywalk, with visitors watching from the walkway and misty hills behind. Official half-day program gallery photo, chosen over the listed candidates as more place-specific: (4) is an aerial of the walkway with no elephants, (9) is a close-up of two elephants. The original is about 5 MB, so I used the site's ?w=1280 resize.

The distillery's thatched open-air bar-restaurant beside its sugarcane field, with soft-focus garden plants in front. This is the og:image of The Distillery Phuket ('Home of Chalong Bay'), the official venue site that the Chalong Bay distillery-visit page links to for booking. The listed og:image (fb.jpg) was rejected as a text-heavy bottle-and-logo promo. The chalongbayrum.com gallery images are only 496x320, and the CC photos on Flickr (2015) are dull and dated.

Candidate 1. Banana Beach cove at sunrise (Dec 2017): sand, surf, rocks and the wooded headland. Geotagged 8.0424, 98.2766. Sharp, no watermark. The author asks to be credited as 'Photo: Anton Zelenov'.

Found by search. The classic view down onto the turquoise Laem Singh cove from the roadside viewpoint, with the Kamala headland behind (Apr 2015). Geotagged 7.96997, 98.27943. Natively 16:9. Better than candidate 1 (dated 2007 shot with a thin frame border). Candidate 2 was rejected: blurred through branches and probably not this beach.
Candidate 1. Ya Nui cove and its rocky islet seen from the Windmill Viewpoint (Jun 2018). 4:3, with the beach mid-frame, so a centred 16:9 crop keeps it.

Found by search. White sand and calm water on Tri Trang Beach, looking across Patong Bay (Apr 2015). Geotagged 7.88664, 98.27161, inside OSM's Tri Trang Beach outline (the file is titled 'Patong' after the photo series). Natively 16:9. Rejected: candidate 1 (construction hoarding), 2 (dark night shot), 3 (©Phuket 101 watermark, blog image).
Candidate 1. Ao Yon Beach: curved sand and a calm, clear bay towards Cape Panwa (Nov 2023). Natively 16:9 and sharp.

Candidate 1. Horse riders on Layan Beach in the late afternoon, with the round islet at the north end (Jun 2022). 4:3, with subjects mid-frame, so it survives a 16:9 crop. Candidate 2 has a Phuket 101 watermark.

Weakest pick. Palms, a yellow Thai sala and the sea on the Sai Kaew beach road (Apr 2015). Geotagged 8.18473, 98.28925, about 500 m south of OSM's Sai Kaew Beach viewpoint. Taken from a moving car: slight motion blur at full size and a faint glare streak top-right, but it reads fine at card size. Rejected: candidate 1 (road), 2 (motion-blurred), 3 (large Willy Thuan watermark). Search covered Commons geo and text in English and Thai, plus Openverse; the Commons 'Sai Kaew Beach' category is the Pattaya one. Found by Thai-name search. Grassy slopes of Laem Krating cape above the rocky shore and turquoise sea (Sep 2020). The file title means 'Laem Krating, Phuket'. CROPPED by me to 16:9 (rows 100-820 of the 1280x960 thumbnail) to remove a small 'Phuket Guide by Phukhao' corner logo. This is a derivative, so the credit should say 'cropped'. The candidate (thaiholidayguide.com aerial) was rejected: soft, third-party site, location and rights unverifiable.

Found by search. View of Chalong Bay from the Kao Khad scenic viewpoint (Nov 2023). Shows the view, not the tower itself. Geotagged at the same spot as the author's photo of the 'Kao-Khad Views Point' sign. 2:1 panorama; a centred 16:9 crop (1138x640) keeps the bay. Candidate 1 is only 640x480 (2010); candidate 2 is a wider 2.6:1 panorama of the same view.
Candidate 1. Hong Kong Airlines A320 (B-LPV) on final approach low over Mai Khao Beach, with plane spotters on the sand (Apr 2025). Geotagged at the runway-end beach. Sharp.

From the official site (the item's website, the Bang Rong community-based tourism site). Drone view of the Bang Rong mangrove channel with fish-farm rafts and Phang Nga Bay hills behind. Natively 16:9, no watermark. The candidate (2007 Commons harbour photo by Tuderna) is sky-heavy with a thin frame, and Commons has no other Bang Rong photos.

Official GRP photo of a rescued gibbon eating fruit beside its forest enclosure fence. The listed candidate (1-hour.png) was rejected because it is a square promo graphic with large text and a BOOK button. Commons has no photos of the project; this one came from the site's media library.

No watermark, free licence, landscape (almost 16:9). It shows the Koh Sirey monkey viewing point: macaques on the mangrove mudflat beside the island road at about 17:00 (Flickr title 'Les singes de 17 h 00. Ko Sire.', Mar 2014). Commons has nothing for Koh Sirey: its 'Wat Ko Si Re' category holds Nai Harn photos, and geotagged files nearby are other places. The only CC photo of the hilltop temple is a portrait, and a 16:9 crop cuts its subject (hnmntn, CC BY-NC 2.0, golden hamsa pillar above the naga stairs: https://www.flickr.com/photos/193313739@N02/53120088126/). phuket101 photos are watermarked. No official or TAT page photo was found. Heads-up for the guide text: Thai news clips from about a year ago (ThaiPBS, Ch7) report that the temple's golden-rock (Kyaiktiyo) replica was closed after a landslide damaged its pavilion. No watermark. It's Wat Karon (Wat Suwan Khiri Khet), the temple whose grounds hold the market: the red-and-gold ordination hall with its long green naga balustrade on a blue stone base, palms and hills behind. The NC licence is fine for a personal guide. No free-licensed photo of the market itself exists. Candidate 1: the Kruvit Raft deck at dusk, with diners under lit roofs over the water (the page confirms it is Kruvit Raft). A small ©WillyThuan mark at the bottom-left falls outside a centred 16:9 crop. The official site kruvitraft.com is unreachable and Commons has no photos.

The cafe's own photo, with no watermark: the hillside deck with wooden low tables, floor cushions and a cushioned bench, looking down on a turquoise bay full of anchored yachts, framed by tree branches. It's image 3 of 20 in the cafe's pinned garden-and-sea-view post (3 Mar 2026). It's portrait (1080x1262), but I checked a centred 16:9 crop: it keeps the yachts and the deck tables and cushions. Fallback from the same post: image 2, the open deck with cushion rows facing the bay between two headlands (also portrait).

Candidate 1: the hilltop terrace with rattan seating and a wide view over Chalong and the bay. A small '© Phuket 101' mark and a thin stitched strip run along the bottom edge; both fall outside a centred 16:9 crop. No official site was found, only booking listings.

The classic view of the Ko Tapu rock pillar ('James Bond Island') with a longtail boat, the Khao Phing Kan cliffs, blue sky and green water. This is candidate 2. Candidate 1 was rejected: grey overcast sky and the Ko Tapu pillar is not visible.

Official tour photo: a guided yellow John Gray 'Sea Canoe' paddling among the Phang Nga Bay limestone rocks. It is the tour page's og:image (candidate 2), saved as the full 2048px original instead of the 1024px resize. Candidate 1 was rejected: an old, soft 768px photo.

Maya Bay seen from the beach (March 2026): turquoise water between sheer cliffs, with boats moored at the mouth of the bay. Chosen over candidate 1, a sharp 2013 photo that shows longtail boats pulled up on Maya Beach. Boats can no longer land there since the 2022 reopening. Candidate 1 is a fine fallback: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 3.0.

Donald Duck Bay on Ko Similan (island #8), seen from the Sail Rock viewpoint: white beach, bright turquoise bay, granite boulders, moored yachts. Found by searching Commons. Candidate 1 was rejected: a hazy 2.4:1 panorama whose 16:9 crop cuts off the beach and half a person at the edge. Candidate 2 was rejected: a generic 1024px beach shot.
Sharp 2024 drone shot of Racha Yai's main bay (Patok Bay): white sand, turquoise water, the pier, moored boats and resort gardens. Candidate 1 accepted. Candidate 2 shows only open sea.

Beach on Koh Hey (Coral Island): white sand, clear green water, swimmers and speedboats, with the Phuket coast across the water. The same Flickr photo is used as the Wikivoyage Coral Island banner. The source file has black letterbox bars, so the saved file is a 1280x720 centre crop of the 1280x960 thumbnail with the bars removed. Both candidates were rejected: #1 is a stormy longtail shot that could be any beach, #2 is a sunset with no island.
Koh Khai Nok: the rocky islet with its colourful beach bar on stilts above white sand and rocks, under a bright sky. Candidate 1 accepted.

The island's signature view: limestone rocks rising from calm Phang Nga Bay, seen from Koh Yao Noi on a soft, hazy day. Reads well as a 16:9 card. Candidate 1 accepted. Commons has few photos of the island itself (only hazy beach or sunrise shots).

Koh Hong (Krabi) beach: a large rock and two rock islets framing turquoise water with swimmers. It is a 2.47:1 panorama. The 16:9 centre crop (about 923px wide) keeps both rock formations and the beach. Candidate 1 accepted.

Railay West beach with a row of longtail boats at the water's edge and the Railay limestone cliffs behind. The image is about 1.95:1 and survives a 16:9 crop. Candidate 1 accepted. Candidate 2 is dominated by sunbathers.

Limestone karst island rising out of Cheow Lan Lake's teal water under a blue sky, with a longtail boat. This is candidate 2. I picked it over candidate 1 (a lone dead tree in the lake) because it is more recognizable. The island fits a centered 16:9 crop.

Golden sunrise over Phang Nga Bay's karst islands seen from the Samet Nangshe viewpoint (2018-04-14, 06:19, Wiki Loves Earth). It fits the sunrise visit. Both candidates were rejected: c1 is portrait with the bay in the lower third, and c2 has a heavy painterly filter.

Official party photo of Halfmoon Festival's jungle stage at Ban Tai at night: psychedelic decor, lasers and a big crowd. A small Halfmoon logo sits in the top ~6%, so a centered 16:9 crop removes it. Rejected: candidate 1 (a text-heavy 2026 date-calendar graphic), and Phasawan viewpoint and the Hat Rin aerial (no party). It differs from the Full Moon Party event photo.

Candidate 1: One Chun's restored Sino-Portuguese shophouse at night, with its 'One Chun' sign, green shutters and diners at the door. Sharp. A centered 16:9 crop keeps the sign and entrance. The Michelin candidate shows only a dish.

This is the cover photo from the restaurant's own Facebook page (facebook.com/meetonpoe, which OSM also lists as its website). It is an overhead shot of their signature Phuket Hokkien noodles: a gravy noodle bowl with egg yolk, seafood, pork and greens, served in a rooster bowl on the shop's branded paper printed with the 林 logo. Raw noodles, shallots, chives and pork crackling sit beside it. The photo is sharp and landscape, with no watermark. A 16:9 centre crop (960x540) keeps the whole bowl. 960 px is the largest size Facebook serves. The fbcdn link is signed and expires around 19 Oct 2026, but the file is saved locally. Rejected: the given candidate (a generic Hokkien mee photo from Bangkok, not this shop), the page's logo-only profile picture, and its 9 recent posts (portrait Vegetarian Festival procession shots). Searched with nothing usable: Wikimedia Commons (English and Thai names, Hokkien mee Phuket, and photos geotagged within 500 m of the main branch at the Surin Circle clock tower) and Openverse/Flickr CC (several spellings). Those turned up only generic Hokkien mee from other cities and shots of the clock tower. Phuket101's photos are third-party and all rights reserved, so I left them out. No official website exists (meetonpoe.com / .co.th do not resolve).

Sharp shot of por pia sod (fresh Phuket spring rolls in sweet sauce) at Lock Tien food court. The Flickr caption confirms the venue, and the owner asks for credit to 'Streets of Food and www.streetsoffood.com'. It was taken at the old Yaowarat/Dibuk corner before the 2025 move to Bangkok Road; it shows only the dish, so it isn't misleading. No candidates were given; Commons has no Lock Tien photos, and Openverse and Flickr have only this one.

Go Benz at night (2021-12-03 20:11): red 'Go Benz rice soup Phuket Original' signboard, cooks at the counter, busy tables, Michelin 2019 sticker. I picked it over the Michelin og:image (a rice-soup bowl) because it shows the place. The license is non-commercial and no-derivatives: fine for this personal guide shown with CSS crop or resize, but don't save an edited copy. If a non-ND image is needed, use https://prod-pics.guide.michelin.com/api/public/content/6ed352d69f8a452eb765d302d1c55a83.jpeg?format=jpeg&w=1000&h=1000

Candidate 1, the Michelin og:image: Southern Thai prawns with sator beans and chilli in red curry sauce at Naam Yoi. Sharp; the square format keeps the dish in a centered 16:9 crop. The other two gallery shots are an overhead spread (crops badly) and an empty dining room. No CC photos on Commons, Flickr or Openverse. The Commons kaeng som candidate is generic.

Clam soup with holy basil and shallots, from Mor Mu Dong's own Michelin gallery. I chose it over the og:image candidate (fried pork belly) to suit a mangrove seafood restaurant. Sharp; the square format keeps the bowl's centre in 16:9. All 6 gallery images are dishes; no venue (mangrove huts) photo exists there or as CC on Commons, Flickr or Openverse.

Entrance to Malin Plaza night market on Prachanukhro Road at night (2025-09-03): lit food stalls, string lights, signboard. The upload title says Malin night market and its geotag is ~110 m from the market. The top third is dark sky, so a bottom-weighted 16:9 crop is best. No candidates were given; found by Commons geosearch. Flickr's Malin Plaza photos aren't CC, and the CC 'Patong night market' photos are Banzaan, not Malin.

Patong Bay seen from the Kalim-end rocks: turquoise water and the full sweep of Patong Beach with umbrellas, Patong Tower and the hills. Picked over candidate 1, which passed but is dominated by the paved promenade, and candidate 2, a generic sunset with a photographer watermark.
Candidate 1, confirmed as Kamala Beach by its file description and category: a calm turquoise bay with white sand and the forested north headland with white hillside villas. Native 16:9.
Candidate 1: north end of Surin Beach, with turquoise water, white sand and the rocky, palm-covered headland toward Pansea. Sharp, clear sky.
Candidate 1 (2024, geotagged at Bang Tao): palms and sun loungers on white sand, with the southern headland across turquoise water.
Candidate 1 (geotagged at Layan): three horse riders on the sand at dusk, with the small forested headland at the north end of the beach. The subject survives a 16:9 crop.

Daytime Nai Thon Beach: casuarina-shaded sand, kayaks and the forested north headland under a blue sky. The location comes from the Flickr title (no geotag); the layout matches other Nai Thon photos. Candidate rejected: it carries repeated freepik stock watermarks. Commons has no good daytime shot; the free-licence fallback is the dusk photo File:Naiton_beach_-_panoramio.jpg (CC BY-SA 3.0). The NC licence is fine for a personal guide.
Candidate 1 (Dec 2022, geotagged at Nai Yang): a long sandy curve with the forested southern headland, longtail boats and a small islet under a blue sky.

Mai Khao's signature view (filed in Category:Mai Khao Beach): a Thai Airways jet landing low over the long casuarina-lined beach while visitors watch, under a deep blue sky. Both candidates rejected: one is a foam close-up that could be anywhere, the other is tilted, overcast and centred on a child.

Karon Beach (per its file description and category): clear turquoise shallows with a granite boulder, and the long beach with umbrellas, the hills and Karon's tall hotel tower behind. Both candidates rejected: one is a featureless sand/sea/sky shot, the other is hazy with litter on the sand.

Kata Yai in the morning, looking south: turquoise water and surf, sand, and the tree-covered south headland with beachfront restaurants. Picked over candidate 1, which passed but is dominated by a large shadowed sand-erosion ledge, and candidate 2, which has vines across the frame and may be Kata Noi.

Kata Noi bay seen from the rocks at its south end: turquoise water, the curving beach with the Katathani umbrellas and the wooded headland (geotagged, in the Kata Noi beach category). Both candidates were rejected. c1 is a generic sunset with a woman's silhouette and nothing that marks it as Kata Noi; it is also the places:kata-noi-beach candidate. c2 is a night portrait of a woman on a chair. This photo came from a Commons search.

Nai Harn Beach looking north to The Nai Harn hotel, terraced on the wooded hill; pale hazy sky (candidate 1, passed). A brighter blue-sky option if wanted: File:Nai harn beach phuket (63).jpg by Wolfgang Holzem, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Longtail boats moored off Rawai Beach under a clear sky, with the wooded headland behind (candidate 1, passed). Possible duplicate: this same file is also the first candidate for places:rawai-seafood-market. If that card uses it too, swap one of them.

View from the Big Buddha hill over Chalong town, the road down to Chalong Pier and the bay full of yachts; overcast (candidate 1, passed). The pier and bay are in the upper third, so a crop that sits higher (object-position around 30%) frames it better than a centred crop. Candidate 2 was almost only open water and sky.

Pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses along Thalang Road in Old Phuket Town; cloudy sky, parked cars in front (candidate 1, passed). Candidate 2 (Thalang_Road_3.jpg) is also a candidate for places:sunday-walking-street, so leaving it out here avoids a duplicate.
Kathu Waterfall running over granite boulders in the jungle; sharp and already 16:9 (candidate 1, passed). Saved as .jpg.
Clear, shallow turquoise sea at Cape Panwa with a longtail boat and the offshore islands under a blue sky (candidate 1, passed; geotagged at the cape).

Panorama of the Ao Po pier shore (boats, beacon tower, wooded hills) under big white clouds; a Commons Quality Image (candidate 2). The photo is about 2.2:1, and a centred 16:9 crop keeps the pier. Candidate 1 was rejected for a large FORUM.LINVOYAGE.COM watermark, which the other Ao Po marina yacht photos on Commons also carry.

Aerial view in morning light of Wat Phra Nang Sang, the historic temple in Thalang town, with the town and the Khao Phra Thaeo hills behind (Wiki Loves Monuments 2023; found by a Commons search). All three candidates were rejected. c1, the Heroines Monument at night, is a soft, grainy film scan that is mostly black. c2 shows only the museum's roof and lawn, nothing recognisable. c3 is an unrecognisable forest pond and is also the places:bang-pae-waterfall candidate. Commons has no daytime photo of the Heroines Monument.

Long, empty Natai Beach with casuarina trees and surf, geotagged at Natai; grey monsoon-season sky (candidate 1, passed). Candidate 2 (bababeachclub.com) was rejected: a 700x700 generic beach shot with nothing that places it at Natai, and it would likely repeat on the Baba Beach Club hotel card. Commons searches (Natai, Khok Kloi, Phang-nga Panoramio) found no sunnier free photo.

Signature pool with the round 'flying saucer' swim-up bar, flamingo floats, beachfront villas and the Andaman Sea behind; official Natai gallery slide (native 16:9). Preferred over the 700x700 candidate crops of the same view.

credit: © Aleenta Phuket Phang Nga Resort & Spa
note: Daylight drone view of the white beachfront pool villas on Natai Beach (native 16:9). It was the og:image of the official aleenta.com/phuket/ page; the live site (Cloudflare challenge) dropped it in the 2026 redesign, so the file came from the Wayback copy of 2026-07-17. Candidate Natai Beach area photos rejected because they don't show the resort. Live-site fallback: https://www.aleenta.com/media/gsqlejse/aleenta-phuket-phang-nga-luxury-resort-thailand-exterior-mp-l1007702.jpg?width=1920 (sunset over the resort's infinity pool).

Shows Natai House's own white garden bungalows (rooms 5 and 6) with palms and a blue sky. Comes from the hotel's official Facebook page: a professional photo set posted 3 Aug 2026 in the 'Deluxe garden view room' album. Sharp, 3:2 landscape, so a 16:9 crop loses little. The URL is the full-size og:image Facebook gives for that public photo page. It only serves the image to link-preview crawlers (downloaded with the facebookexternalhit user agent); other bots get a 960 px version. Alternative: the page's current cover photo, a night shot of the pool beside a lit stone bungalow (media_id=1345600507580669, 1996x2015 near-square, but a centred 16:9 crop works). Not chosen because the photo dates from about 2017-2022: the orange wall in it was white by a Dec 2025 photo. Other page photos are interiors, posters or older 979 px shots. Commons has nothing closer than Natai Beach, about 700 m away.

Pool of The Snug wing, shaded by palm trees, with sun loungers (official homepage photo; the site describes the Snug pool as surrounded by palm trees). Chosen over the candidate room-interior share image.

Elevated view over the infinity pool, beach-club pavilion, umbrellas and Kamala Bay through pine trees (official homepage hero). Panorama that crops cleanly to 16:9; chosen over the candidate beach slide, which has a dark gradient baked into the bottom.
Aerial of the orange-accented hotel blocks on the white sand of north Kamala Beach in morning light; the candidate image at 2048 px from Accor's official image CDN.
Long palm-lined main pool leading to the A-frame lobby pavilion (official homepage image; candidate 1).
Sunset aerial of the hotel building with its rooftop infinity pool and Bang Tao Bay behind; the ibis Styles sign is part of the facade. Candidate image at 2048 px from Accor's official CDN.
Open-sided luxury safari tent with bed and swing daybed among casuarina trees, beach visible behind (official site; candidate 1).
Street facade at dusk with the Hotel Indigo sign, boat sculpture, ornate lamp posts and a large banyan tree (official homepage hero; candidate 1, desktop version; the mobile duplicate was deleted).

credit: © Holiday Inn Express Phuket Patong Beach Central
note: Pool courtyard with umbrellas and the hotel's purple-framed wings in tropical greenery (native 16:9, IHG gallery image for hotel code PHUEX). ihg.com returns 403, so the image IDs came from the Wayback copy of the hotel page (2025-10-10); the file is served live by IHG's image CDN. The candidate Patong Beach area photo was rejected.

Daytime view of the long pool beside the white hostel wings, spiral staircase and lounge area (official slider photo on the Lub d Phuket Patong page, 2020-2021). lubd.com returns 403 to every request, so the file came from the Wayback copy; the 2025 site hero shows the same pool and building. The candidate Bangla Road and Patong Beach area photos were rejected.
Aerial of the resort's lagoon pool and Thai-pavilion pool bar opening onto Kata Beach (official homepage gallery). Listed candidate 10-1.jpg rejected: 600x1300 portrait, too narrow.
Aerial of the villas on the rocky headland above Kata Noi beach, with Kata and Karon bays behind (first candidate, official site).

credit: © Sugar Marina Hotel ART Karon Beach
note: Aerial of the hotel's pixel-art tiled pool, mushroom splash park and white pool-access wing (official site gallery). Candidate og image rejected: mostly two fashion models posing in front of the sign.
Aerial of the white terraced hotel on the green hillside above Nai Harn bay (official og:image, exactly 16:9).

credit: © Wyndham Grand Nai Harn Beach Phuket
note: Lagoon pool courtyard between the resort's residence blocks under blue sky (official property gallery, 52543_pool_view_20). Chosen over the candidate entrance-sign photo (exterior_view_1), which also passed but is less representative.
Canvas bell tent with open door and cosy interior in a sunlit tropical garden (first candidate, official site). Alternative on the same site: 1665046558tent-3.png (row of tents).
White Sino-Portuguese arcaded facade of the hotel (no. 26), with one guest posing at the entrance (first candidate). The other slideshow images are interiors and the small pool.

The hotel's hanging 'The Memory at On On hotel, Phuket Old Town' signboards on Phang Nga Road, with the white colonial Kasikorn Bank building filling most of the frame. Official site has only a grainy sepia archive photo, banners with dark text overlays, and a 359px modern facade thumbnail.

The hotel itself, as asked: the white Sino-Portuguese shophouse facade at 56 Krabi Road. It shows the red 'SHUNLI HOSTEL' sign with its phone number, the arched balconies, and the black-and-gold 順利 (Shunli) signboard with house number 56 over the entrance. Sharp, bright, 3:2, and a centred 16:9 crop keeps both signs. It's from the property's own gallery on Booking.com ('Shunli Hotel - SHA Extra Plus', 75 photos), not a guest upload. There's no official website, and the Facebook page (Shunlihostelphuket) only shows its sign logo to visitors who aren't logged in. Alternatives from the same gallery: the entrance with open doors under the 順利 sign (id 107324272), the lobby (107324279) and rooms (380493360). The old Thalang Road area photo was replaced.

Beachfront pool with a large thatched sala and loungers, sea and mountains behind (official homepage gallery). Candidate 1942.jpg (white cottages in a garden) also passed but is less representative. The og-images aerial makes the resort tiny, and the Commons Ban Tai photo is overcast.

AREA PHOTO, not the hostel itself: Ban Tai Beach at sunset with palms (hostel is about 900 m inland). No official website or social page found and nothing on Commons. Booking.com and Agoda block scraping, and the Hostelworld listing (312348) now returns 404, so the hostel may be delisted or closed; worth re-checking. Candidate Ban_Tai_Beach_Ko_Pha_Ngan.jpg rejected as dull and overcast.

Guests on pink and yellow loungers at the pool terrace in front of the hostel's lilac building. It is the og:image of the official Koh Phangan beachfront hostel page, the same photo appears in the property's Hostelworld gallery, and the lilac building is visible from the entrance. Candidate Cloudbeds 10-bed dorm photo also passed. Rejected an official 'baan tai pic 6' pool photo whose pool does not match the property's other photos.

The shopfront, from the company's own About Us page: a big green 'Mamy Exchange' sign with 'CURRENCY EXCHANGE / ОБМЕН ВАЛЮТ / 外币兑换', the glass storefront and steps, and the 'Mamy Booking / Mamy Exchange Co., Ltd.' pylon beside it. It's the company's only office (9/10 Moo 4, Koh Kaew, on the airport road). Daylight, sharp, 4:3, and a centred 16:9 crop keeps the whole sign. Found through the site's WordPress media library. The homepage og:image is only the SVG logo, and the other uploads are banners or flags.

The actual Lion Currency Exchange booth at Jungceylon, Patong (The Botanica Zone, GF unit GC4118): lit CURRENCY EXCHANGE sign, LION logo and a rate screen. Sharp, no watermark. Taken from Jungceylon's official mall directory page for Lion. Lion's own Facebook page shows 'content isn't available' when logged out, and Commons has nothing for it.

Shopfront of the 'SuperRich Partner Phuket' branch on Ratsada Rd at Suriyadej Circle: orange EXCHANGE sign and SPR 'Currency Exchange' standee. This is the branch's featured image in the official superrich1965.com branch data (record phuket-suriyadej-circle-superrich-partner). The filename ends in '-gmap', so SuperRich probably took it from the branch's Google Maps listing; swap it if that matters. 4:3, so the top of the sign gets tight in a centered 16:9 crop; top-aligned works better. Fallback: Commons 'SuperRich currency exchange in Dusit Central Park (2026).jpg' (CC BY 4.0), but that is a Bangkok branch.

STREET PHOTO, not the office. No photo of NC Plus exists in open or official sources: it has no website, I found no reachable Facebook page, and Commons searches (English, Thai, and a geosearch along the road) found nothing. This shows Thilok Uthit 2 Rd (OSM 'Tilokuthit 2 Road') looking north toward Khao Rang hill, about 190 m north of the office (OSM node 5520221423 'NC'). It is a Jan 2021 KartaView street-level frame that I cropped to 16:9 to remove the car dashboard and windscreen pillar. CC BY-SA 4.0 requires saying it was modified. Plates are privacy-blurred.

Official photo of a Value Plus booth: lit Value+Plus sign, red CURRENCY EXCHANGE counter and a rate screen. Sharp, professional. The photo does not say which branch it is (probably a mall branch). The site's branch API confirms this is the same chain as the Phuket booths (Patong, Laguna, Central Festival Phuket and others).

Money Shop's Kata office (64/5 Kata Rd): yellow and black CURRENCY EXCHANGE / MONEY SHOP shopfront with a pole sign. Sharp, professional, no watermark. I matched it to the Kata entry using the layout positions in the official site's office list. Some signage is in Russian. The site also has photos of the Rawai, Nai Harn and Chalong Lotus's offices.

Generic image: a purple Siam Commercial Bank 'Currency Exchange' booth with an electronic rate board and tourists queuing (Suvarnabhumi Airport, Bangkok, 2007). An older compact-camera shot, slightly soft but fine at card size. Phuket alternative: Commons 'File:Bank of Ayudhya Phuket.jpg' (public domain, a Krungsri branch exchange window in Rawai, 2010, no rate board visible).

A row of six Thai bank ATMs (TMB, SCB, Krungthai, Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, Thanachart) inside Phuket International Airport, April 2017. Sharp, 16:9. This shows ATMs, not the exchange counters: Commons has no photo of the HKT exchange counters (I checked the airport's category tree for 2016-2025 and searched in English and Thai). The official AOT site lists the counters but shows no photos. This is the most money-related terminal shot available.

Found by searching Commons. All 3 candidates were rejected: #1 is hazy with litter on the sand, #2 is a sunset that could be any beach, #3 is overcast and dull. This photo shows surf sweeping up Karon's long beach under a blue sky with clouds, with swimmers, the green headland and Karon's tall white tower. It is a different photo and composition from the area card (Thailande 2010 259, the boulder shot). Sharp; the 16:9 crop only trims sky and sand.

Found in the Commons category 'Kamala beach'. All 3 candidates were rejected: #1 is mostly sky with distant boats and a thin frame border, #2 is a generic top-down drone shot of longtail boats, #3 is a gloomy dusk scene with a tiki torch. This photo shows surf breaking on Kamala Beach under a deep blue sky, with the conical green hill and its hillside villas behind the bay. It is clearly different from the area card (Thailande 2010 248, the calm headland). Wide 1.94:1 image, so the 16:9 crop only trims the sides.

Skipped candidate 1 (Surin_Beach.JPG) because the areas:surin card already uses it. Rejected candidate 2, a portrait sunset with a red flag that could be any beach. Found this one by searching Commons for the Thai name: 'Mittraphap thi Hat Surin' (Friendship at Surin Beach), a Wiki Loves Earth 2022 upload. It shows Surin's wide sunny beach with swimmers, surf and the wooded headland with hotels under a blue sky, a different end and view from the area card. Phone photo with mild HDR; there is a small red flag mid-beach.

Candidate 1: the stadium's sunny daytime front with its big 'BANGLA BOXING STADIUM / THAI BOXING STADIUM / REAL FIGHT' sign and boxer statues. The sign stays readable in a 16:9 crop at card size; there are vehicles at the bottom edges. Commons has only these 3 files. The official site has only a composited hero graphic and text-heavy fight posters. #2 is a duller front view under grey sky, and #3 (a boxer with his trainer) does not show it is Bangla.

Candidate 2: a sharp, close view of the yellow Sino-Portuguese mansion on Krabi Road that houses the Blue Elephant restaurant and cooking school. 'BLUE ELEPHANT' is lettered over the door, with traveller's palms and a lawn in front. #1 is the same building far across the lawn under grey sky; #3 is just the logo.

Candidate 1, from the official homepage: the indoor ice bath and hot tub, with '12° Ice Tub' and '43° Hot tub' signs, hanging plants and a timber-look ceiling. The image is nearly square, but I checked that a centred 16:9 crop keeps both pools and the signs. The site confirms its single location near Boat Avenue in Bangtao. #2 shows the café bar, not the sauna; the site's other images are square sauna, lounge or model shots; #3 is a portrait shot from a third-party guide site.

Official og:image: the venue's covered hillside terrace with bean bags and guests watching the sunset over the Andaman Sea. It is a real photo with heavy color grading, and the venue's own Google profile posted the same photo. The image is wider than 16:9 (1.94:1), so a center crop only trims the sides. Rejected: the Megatix cover (neon LEVITATE logo graphic) and a second Megatix image (AI-style floating-island illustration). The other images on the site are decorative backgrounds.

Roger Sanchez DJ set at Armania (Jan 2025): the arched DJ booth with the Armania logo, gold light beams and a crowd with hands up. This is the full-size original of candidate 1 (the listed URL was the 1024px resize), and it is used on the official Armania page. There is a small DJ name sign on the booth and no watermark. Candidate 2 (an aerial hoop performer) is also good but shows less of the club.

license: venue's own photo (its EBS Matchstaff venue profile)
note: Inside Summerset Lounge (Wana Park, Cherngtalay) at night: the bar with its yellow sun disc, tufted leather sofas and red curtains. Homepage hero photo, original JPEG: a wide view of the open-air club with the DJ booth framed by tropical plants, red and blue lasers, hanging light tubes and a crowd in front. No watermark. Rejected candidates: DSC_1424 (close-up of one dancing guest with a Sound Club logo watermark) and DSC07753 (dark red silhouette that doesn't show the venue). All of the roughly 590 gallery photos carry the logo watermark.

Portrait phone photo of a Seaside beach party at night: the crowd at the DJ booth, with a fire dancer over the dark sea behind. A Saturday-night crowd dancing with arms raised under string lights inside Hollystone. Hollystone Phangan posted it on its own Facebook page. Backup if wanted: a sharper photo of the DJ booth under its thatched roof, https://www.welove-kohphangan.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/327310897_830640868036202_6058009428823177000_n.jpg (1440x959). An aerial night shot of the Utopia jungle rave: the arched-truss stage, green lasers and smoke over a packed crowd, with the rock wall and jungle behind. Candidate 1 (a daytime venue shot from phangan.events, 1280x589) also passes but is softer and less striking. Candidate 2 is a flyer covered in text.

Nai Thon Beach by day: wide golden sand, a row of umbrellas and loungers, turquoise sea and the forested north headland under a blue sky. The photo is geotagged on the beach. This is candidate 1 (the 1280x1707 portrait thumbnail), cropped to 16:9 (rows 800-1520) so the beach fills the card instead of empty sky. The crop is a modification under CC BY-SA. It is a different photo from the area card (the Flickr tnocapital shot taken from the casuarina shade with kayaks). Candidate 2 (pink dusk with rocks) is a good backup. Rejected: File:Naithon-beach-wooden-bridge.jpg, which carries repeated freepik stock watermarks. note: Inside the airport branch: a rock waterfall wall with the green 'NATURAL Restaurant' sign, boat-shaped wooden booths around a pond, and plants everywhere. The shop front, with the 'Sabai Phuket MASSAGE - Phuket Airport' sign and the number 18/18, which matches the branch address (18/18 Moo 1, Sakhu). Three white loungers under two thatched umbrellas next to the hostel's pool, in daylight. This is candidate 1, accepted. Tiled pool in front of the white hotel block, with palms and the garden on the right. This is the full-size original of candidate 1 (2121x1100x500.jpg is the same photo made smaller). It is a phone panorama of about 2.2:1, so the 16:9 crop trims the sides; I checked the crop and it still shows the pool and building. Candidate 2 (a room) is soft. The other site photos are rooms, the lobby, a street view with power lines, and a building-and-garden shot (2122.jpg) as a backup.

Long pool with orange umbrellas and loungers, the hotel block behind it, and one guest sitting at the pool edge. This is candidate 1, accepted: a sharp professional photo used on the official homepage. Candidate 2 is the entrance with the logo sign, and candidate 3 is the lobby.

Pulley Pool & Bar in daylight: a dark-wood Thai pavilion bar over a green-tiled pool, with palms and The Slate's tyre sculptures. It comes from the official pools page. Candidates 2 and 3 (pool villas from above, a suite balcony) show less of the resort. Backup: the dusk version of the same pool, Pulley-Pool-Bar---Cover.jpg.

There were no candidates. This is an aerial photo from the item's website (the pier page, captioned 'Phuket Rassada Pier').
