The other Commons ground photo shows only the entrance with vans.

Found by Commons search; it is from the same September 2025 series as candidate 1 and geotagged at the pier. It shows Chalong Pier with its roofed jetty building on the left, speedboats and longtails in front and the yacht anchorage behind, under a cloudy sky. Candidate 1 shows the pier small at the left edge and is mostly water. Candidate 2 (the view from Big Buddha) is already used for areas:chalong.

Found by Commons search (Rawai Beach category). It shows the long concrete Rawai pier on the right, two longtail boats with Thai flags and a speedboat, with islands behind (2010, overcast). Candidate 1 was rejected: it is a close-up of the red 'Rawai Landing Pier' sign, which is mostly text. This is a different file from the one used for areas:rawai (Rawai Beach 11).

Found by Commons search. It shows the very long Ao Po pier with lamp posts running across the frame, and a speedboat and a longtail in the shallow bay (May 2011). The geotag is at the shore end of the pier and matches the pier line in OpenStreetMap. Candidate 1 (Diego Delso's panorama) is already used for areas:ao-po, and it is a view from the pier, not of it.

From the slideshow on the official homepage. It is a sunny aerial view of the marina pontoons full of yachts and superyachts, with the wooded headland and the Phang Nga Bay hills behind. No watermark. Candidate 1 was rejected: it is a close-up of outboard engines at a boat show with a large 'FORUM.LINVOYAGE.COM' watermark.

From the media library of the Bang Rong community tourism site; the photo is attached to its Bang Rong page. It is a drone view of Bang Rong Pier: the jetty with parked cars and moored speedboats, the long floating raft restaurant and the mangrove channel out to Phang Nga Bay. It is natively 16:9 and sharp. It is a different photo from the one used for places:bang-rong-mangroves (forest-4). Candidate 1 (Tuderna, Commons) was rejected: it shows mangroves and sky with only two boat bows at the edge, not the pier, and has a thin frame.

There were no candidates. This is the only real photo I found: Commons geosearch found it, while Commons text search, Flickr and Openverse had nothing. It shows the long Laem Hin pier on the left with a wooden passenger boat, and the wooden deck of the Laem Hin Seafood restaurant on the right, looking out to the islands (June 2011). The geotag is on that deck, next to the shore end of the 'Laem Hin Pier' line in OpenStreetMap. The sky is hazy and a bit cyan, but the photo is sharp, and the 16:9 centre crop keeps both piers and the boat. The weakest of the 11 picks, but acceptable.

Candidate 1, the homepage og:image. It shows yachts in the marina basin with the marina's white residence buildings and palms behind, under a blue dusk sky. It is about 2:1, and the 16:9 centre crop keeps the yachts and the buildings. A backup on the same site is the newer main slide (MainSlideRPM-scaled.jpg, a 2048x704 sunset aerial).

There were no candidates. Found by Commons geosearch: the geotag is 17 m from the Tap Lamu Pier point in OpenStreetMap. It shows dive and tour boats at the pier (a South Siam Divers speedboat, a red speedboat and two liveaboard ships) with people on the jetty, blue sky and forest behind (March 2015). It is natively 16:9 and sharp. The file title does not name the pier, but the location and the Similan dive boats fit. Flickr options were rejected: stormy fishing-boat shots.

Candidate 2. It shows the long roofed walkway of Klong Jilad Pier with a ferry docked at its end and Krabi's limestone cliffs behind, under a blue sky (Nov 2015). It is geotagged across the water from the terminal. Candidate 1 was rejected: it shows a navy ship and a government building beside a small jetty, not the passenger pier.

Found by Commons search; it is geotagged at the pier. It shows colourful longtail boats and a row of speedboats at Nopparat Thara pier, with the pier buildings and tall limestone cliffs behind, under a blue sky (Feb 2016). Candidate 1 (Jukka) was rejected: it is hazy and half the frame is empty sand.

East Railay bay in June 2018. The long floating pier crosses the middle of the frame: a pontoon walkway with white posts, longtails moored along it and a ferry at its end (checked by zooming into the original). The karst headland is behind. The sky is overcast. It is the only Commons photo that shows the floating pier, and Openverse found nothing closer. The visitthailandtoday pier photos are Google Maps user photos, so they were not used.

Big ferries moored at Ton Sai Pier below the limestone cliffs, with travellers on the pier and the beach in front. Sharp and sunny. The file is in the Commons 'Ton Sai Pier' category. It is an older photo (Nikon D40 era, undated) and the pier deck has been rebuilt since, but the view is the same. Chosen over the given candidates: the bay overview from the hill (pier tiny) and the 2025 longtail shot (no ferries).

Saladan Pier arrival point, Jan 2014: the 'Welcome to Ko Lanta' arch at the pier entrance, with resort staff holding hotel signs and tuk-tuks waiting. Already 16:9. There were no candidates. Commons only has the Saladan waterfront and the Lanta bridge under construction, none clearly the ferry pier, so this Flickr CC photo was used. Earlier waves already used Flickr NC licences.

Standing on Manoh Pier (geotagged on the pier at the south tip of Koh Yao Noi, Jan 2009). The concrete pier leads to the red-roofed buildings and wooded hill on shore, under blue sky. The shore buildings match a 2014 Roma Neus photo of Manoh taken from the water. Slightly soft phone photo, but clear at card size. The pier has more lamp posts now.

From the pier's own website (home-page slider). It shows the red boat-bow terminal at the head of Chong Lard Pier with its Thai sign 'เกาะยาวใหญ่' (Koh Yao Yai), motorbikes on the pier deck, and the sea and hills behind. A small person in white stands under the arch. I checked that this is Chong Lard and not Klong Hia. The same terminal, with 'KOH YAO YAI' on its side, is in the site's chong-lard-pier1-8 gallery photos. Klong Hia's own site (klonghiapier.com) shows a different T-shaped pier with a blue floating pontoon. A 640x360 attention-crop preview keeps the terminal, the pier deck and the sea. Rejected: Commons has no photo of this pier. The CC0 Unsplash 'Koh Yao Yai Peer' shows a resort jetty with Thai lanterns. The 2014 Panoramio shot across the channel most likely shows Manoh Pier. The Flickr 'pier' shots are NC-licensed portraits of people. Ferry-site images are 422 px or are stock photos. Alternative from the same site: images/gallery/chong-lard-pier5.jpg (800x533) shows the whole pier on its piles from the water.

A colourful longtail moored in clear shallow water on Pattaya Beach, Koh Lipe (title says Pattaya Beach; April 2014), blue sky, no people. This is the beach where ferries and speedboats land passengers. The given 'Debarking Ferry' candidate was rejected: it is portrait, faces fill the frame and a 16:9 crop cuts heads. Different from the Sunrise Beach sandbar already used for places:koh-lipe. Phuketian.S photos were skipped because of their 'FORUM linvoyage.com' watermark.

Pier frames at the Bangrak pier cluster on Big Buddha Beach, with the Big Buddha statue on its islet and sailboats behind. Feb 2015, already 16:9. Geotag 9.5594, 100.0575 is beside the Lamtaen terminal and about 200 m from the Lomprayah and Haad Rin Queen (Big Buddha) piers, per OSM. The given candidate was rejected: a girl in a hammock on the ferry, no pier visible.

Aerial photo of a red-and-white Seatran Discovery ferry docked at Seatran's Bangrak Pier, with the beach and hillside behind. Sharp, bright, 16:9, no watermark. Shown on the operator's homepage and About page (file name says Samui Bangrak pier). A 2013 Commons photo from the same spot shows the same pier with the same lantern posts.

Nathon Pier deck, with railing, lamp posts and shelters, leading to the Seahorse car ferry 'The Blue Dolphin' moored there (Commons category Nathon Pier, May 2023). Wide frame; the sides crop away for 16:9. The given 'View from Nathon Pier' was rejected: beach at low tide, pier not visible.

A red-and-white express ferry arriving at Thong Sala Pier while two pier staff watch from the concrete pier, side-on. Turquoise water, soft light, Dec 2014, Commons category Thong Sala Pier. The given candidate was rejected: mostly the 'Multipurpose Port of Koh Phangan' sign. Seatran's own Thong Sala aerial is only 637 px wide.

Hillside view over Haad Rin Nai bay and town. The long Haad Rin (Haadrin Queen) pier reaches into the sea at the end of the beach, with longtails at anchor (titled 'Haad Rin Pier', Dec 2010). Chosen over the given candidate, a close-up of the ferry's side where the pier is not visible, and over a 2003 800 px film scan.

Raja Ferry Pier at Don Sak, June 2022. Several Raja car ferries (one shows the RAJA logo) are moored at the pier under limestone hills. Sharp and bright. The image is wide (2.1:1), so the 16:9 crop only trims the sides and the ferries stay in. I chose it over the listed 2011 photo (Fabio Achilli, one old ferry by a rusty jetty) because it shows the whole port and is newer.

Loh Samah Bay on Phi Phi Leh, where the Maya Bay floating pier is. Taken from the bow of a boat, with longtails on turquoise water between the cliffs. Sharp, no watermark. This was the first listed candidate. I did not use the second (Maya Bay cliffs) because the Phi Phi / Maya Bay card already uses it.

Ko Tapu (James Bond Island) and the islands next to it, with speedboats crossing the bay. A Commons quality image. It is from the same series as the listed DD_30 but wider, and it has speedboats in it. It also looks different from the Phang Nga Bay card, which uses DD_36 (Ko Tapu straight on between cliffs). I did not use the listed Weldon Kennedy photo: it is portrait and is not Ko Tapu. The Simba drone shot is only 870 px wide.

A two-deck tour boat full of passengers in life jackets crossing Phang Nga Bay, with an island behind. Already 16:9, sharp, no watermark. I did not use the listed Ko Panak DD_01 because it shows no boat. The Amazing Canoeing big-boat photo shows the boat with canoes, but it has the company logo in the top-right corner.

Two people paddling their own sea kayak out of a sea cave, with karst islands behind. Commons category: Kayaking in Phang Nga Bay. The exact island is not stated, so it may not be Koh Roi. The kayak survives the 16:9 crop. Paddle Asia's og:image is only 356x356, and all its site photos are under 640 px wide, so none could be used. The listed Weldon Kennedy cave-arch photo shows no paddlers.

The entrance to the Hong Island lagoon in Krabi (the file description says 'Thailand, Krabi, Lagoon of Hong island'), with a longtail and a speedboat coming in. Sharp, no watermark, and different from the Koh Hong (Krabi) card's beach photo. This was the first listed candidate. I rejected the second (DD_18) because it shows souvenir stalls at James Bond Island.

A white-sand beach in the Similan Islands, with turquoise water and tour boats at anchor (a towel and hat in front, a couple walking). The exact island is not stated. Sharp, no watermark. I did not use the listed viewpoint shot because the Similan Islands card already uses it. The other listed Kosin Sukhum shot has no boats, and the Love Andaman image is an operator promo.

Racha Yai's main bay, Dec 2015 (it looks like Patok Bay rather than Siam Bay), seen from the water. Speedboats and dive boats are moored off the white beach and resort, with snorkellers. Already 16:9. The water looks deep blue rather than turquoise. I did not use the listed Nicolas Vollmer photos because they show a beach path and a restaurant with no boats. Phuket Dive Tours has a brighter photo of a speedboat with snorkellers at Racha Yai, but it is square (1078x1078) and the automatic crop cuts out the boat.

Speedboats pulled up on the sand at Khai Nok, with tourists wading ashore through clear water. This is exactly the half-day trip. A Commons quality image. I did not use the listed DD_03 because it is almost the same view as the Khai Islands card (DD_05, the bar on the rocks), and DD_07 shows only rocks. Note that this is Khai Nok, not Khai Nai; the tour visits both.

Longtail boats on the beach at Poda Island, with its rock stack behind (Jan 2012). A Commons quality image. This was the first listed candidate. I rejected the second (Ko Kai & Ko Tub 12) because it is a 1280x368 panorama.

Pileh Lagoon on Phi Phi Leh (matches the Pi Leh Bay map query): speedboats on bright turquoise water under the cliffs. A Commons quality image, no watermark. I did not use the listed Pileh Lagoon 2 because it is dark and mostly cliff. Ko Phi Phi Le 01 shows longtails and is a very wide panorama.

Drone shot of Love Andaman's double-deck catamaran (water slide, parasols on the sun deck) anchored off a green island, with swimmers and a paddleboarder. og:image of its private-charter page (candidate 2). Candidate 1 rejected: PHUKET@PHOTOGRAPHER.NET watermark, and it shows a beach at sunset, not a boat day.

Guest at the bow of Love Andaman's boat watching the sun set over the sea, islands on the horizon. Gallery photo from its Phi Phi + Maiton sunset tour page (same shoot as its sun-deck photos, not stock). Saved as JPEG with the PNG's alpha removed. Rejected: candidate 1 (portrait SUP silhouette, no boat) and candidate 2 (watermark, a beach rather than a boat).

Tour group in red kayaks with a day-trip boat and Ang Thong's limestone islands behind, so it shows the tour itself. Chosen over the Emerald Lake and viewpoint candidates (both acceptable) so this card looks different from the separate places:ang-thong-marine-park card, which will probably get a viewpoint shot. Best viewpoint alternative if wanted: File:Angthong_National_Marine_Park.jpg (Ditsakul, CC BY-SA 3.0). The official og:image is only 700 px, and that site also uses Shutterstock photos.

Klong Khong Beach on Lanta's west coast: calm turquoise water and a palm-lined beach with bungalows. Found by search. The candidates were usable but weaker: (1) mostly bare sand under a pale sky, (2) a generic longtail sunset.

Longtail boats moored in the shallow, very clear turquoise water at Bamboo Island's beach (candidate 3). Rejected: candidate 1 (tsunami sign, portrait) and candidate 2 (crowded 3:1 panorama, too thin for 16:9).

Palms on a white sand spit with turquoise water and green hills behind (looks like the Laem Haad sandbar). Found by search. Chosen over the candidates: (1) a dark HDR beach-bar table and (2) a resort pier at dusk, which shows a resort rather than the island.

The stilt village's waterfront under its huge limestone rock, with a blue sky and a longtail in front (2004, still sharp). A small yellow royal flag sits in the lower right. Found by search. Rejected: candidate 1 (blown-out sky, cluttered), 2 (close-up of the mosque), 3 (restaurant interior).

Chong Khad Bay with clear turquoise water over the reef, a sandy beach and jungle on South Surin, under a cloudy sky (candidate 1). For the Moken village instead: File:Moken_Village1.jpg (same author and license).
White sandbar in turquoise water with a longtail and Koh Adang's hills behind (Sunrise Beach side). Candidate 1, sharp and vivid.

Koh Ngai's white beach with a casuarina tree, turquoise water and limestone islets on the horizon. Found by search. Chosen over the candidates: Emerald Cave (credit watermark, crowded), Kradan (mostly sky) and Ngai (a yacht is the main subject).

Banana Bay, Racha Noi: a forested hill above a granite-boulder shore, very clear blue water and a moored yacht. og:image of the dive operator's Banana Bay page, which the guide cites as a source. It matches other Racha Noi photos (Thai Holiday Guide). Commons has no Racha Noi photos (searched Racha Noi, Raya Noi, the Thai name and Wikidata). Tisland's tour gallery was rejected: generic dolphin photos and views that look like the Similans.

Thong Ta Kian (Crystal Bay / Silver Beach), Koh Samui: white sand, clear turquoise water, granite boulders and a green headland. Native 16:9. Found by a Commons search. Candidate 1 was hazy and dull. Candidate 2 (dusk view over Chaweng Bay) was usable but dark, so a bright daytime beach was preferred.
Candidate 1: the classic viewpoint shot of Koh Nang Yuan, with the white sandbar joining its islets in turquoise water. 4:3, and the subject survives a 16:9 crop.

The iconic panorama from the 350 m viewpoint on Ko Wua Talap: green limestone islands in a turquoise sea. Found by a Commons search. Preferred over the candidates: candidate 1 has small islands on the horizon under mostly sky, and candidate 2 is a close-up of the Emerald Lake lagoon.
Candidate 1: view from the Phi Phi Don viewpoint over Tonsai village and the twin bays with longtail boats, framed by palms. Candidate 2 was rejected because it is a 1280x177 panorama strip.

Candidate 2: the tall limestone rock stack off Koh Poda beach, with kayakers and the Krabi karsts behind. Candidate 1 (Poda beach with a longtail boat) was usable but mostly white sky, so the stronger subject was chosen.

Candidate 1: inside AMP, a wall of vinyl records with hi-fi amps and bottles in warm light. It is portrait and only 750 px wide, but a 16:9 centre crop (checked) keeps the records and amps. No official photos are reachable: the website is Instagram, which only gives a 100 px profile picture. The guide page also has a landscape storefront shot, but its 16:9 crop cuts off the AMP sign and it may be a Google Maps photo, so it was skipped.
Candidate 1, the official site banner (confirmed as its og:image): the cliff-top terrace at a fiery sunset over the sea, with a couple and cocktails at a table.

The jazz band playing in Bebop's new room (moved in 2026 to the 2nd floor of VELA Phuket Old Town, Yaowarat / Phang Nga Road): guitar, singer, sax, drums and a grand piano. It is the og:image of Phuket 101's Bebop page. Same source as candidate 1 (bar counter), but it shows the live music. It has a small "© Phuket 101" mark in the bottom-right corner that falls outside a 16:9 centre crop. Every photo of the new room carries that mark, and the official Facebook page only gives its profile picture without a login.

Candidate 1, the og:image of the guide page (credit "photos by Khun New" confirmed there): an aerial of the Yona floating club in Patong Bay, with its pool, daybeds, palms and upper deck. No watermark. The official site sits behind a Cloudflare check.

From the official homepage gallery: the pool with cabanas, white umbrellas and sunbeds along Bang Tao beach under a blue sky. Chosen over the og:image candidate, a blurred close-up of a lounge sofa that says less about the venue.

Candidate 1: the Baba Nest rooftop deck with striped floor cushions, surrounded by its infinity pool, with the sea and islands beyond in golden-hour light. Candidate 2 shows a different Sri Panwa pool, not Baba Nest.

Candidate 1, the official og:image: a seared-tuna salad with a poached egg on a table at The Kitchen, with the chain's branded menu beside it. Sharp, 4:3, and the 16:9 crop keeps the bowl (checked). The site is shared by the Patong, Lamai and Samui branches and has no photo of the Patong room itself, so this is the brand's own food photo.

Replaces the candidate, a generic Phuket dim sum photo from another shop. This is a table of Chokchai's own Phuket-style dim sum (yellow siu mai, seaweed pork rolls, the red dipping sauce) from a local guide site's July 2020 visit post. The post gives the same address (46/2 Mae Luan Rd) and 04:00-12:00 hours. Sharp, 4:3, no watermark. The shop's Facebook og:image is only its logo, and KTC's copy of its photo is 600x800 portrait.

Inside the cafe, from Phuket Insider's own visit in April 2024 (the same set has a bowl spelling 'INSIDER'). It shows the pink palm-tree wall with 'Fruit Fusion Kamala Cafe' on it, the 'Smoothie Station' neon sign, the swing seat and a table. The photo is portrait. The project's sharp attention crop to 640x360 was tested and keeps the name wall, the neon sign and the table. If you crop by hand, use the upper band starting at about y=150. Tried and rejected: the cafe has no website. The og:image of its Facebook page (fruitfusionofficial) and its Instagram (@fruitfusioncafe) is only the logo, and its Instagram posts could not be reached. The Phuket.Net listing photos are only 600x400 and show the old 2019 interior. Tripadvisor, Wanderlog, coool.cafe and abillion have only Google or user photos. Openverse and Commons have no photo of the cafe, only Kamala Beach shots.

Candidate 1, the official og:image: the poolside lounge terrace with teak and rattan armchairs under a thatched roof. It is portrait, but the 16:9 attention crop keeps the chairs and the pool edge (checked). The site's four other photos and its two videos (720x1280) all show the same lounge, with no banya shot, and no other source is indexed.

Candidate 2, the homepage og:image: a trainer in Bangtao Muay Thai kit doing pad work with a student under the gym's neon 'Bangtao' sign. Chosen over candidate 1 (an MMA team huddle in MMA gloves with nothing that names the gym) because it shows both Muay Thai and the place. Sharp; the 16:9 crop keeps both people and the sign (checked).

From the official Patong page: two surfers on the Patong FlowRider wave, a coach with the tow rope, and onlookers. Behind them are the 'Surf House Pa(tong)' building sign and a 'Surf's up Patong' banner. Sharp and already 16:9. The site's og:image is only the logo.

Hero image 3 from the official site, the same hero set as the two candidates: a smiling rider in an orange helmet on the zipline over green jungle. Chosen over candidate 1 (a group on a tree platform, small figures on a phone card) because it reads clearly at 360 px. Sharp; the 16:9 crop keeps the rider and the cable (checked). The site's blog covers look AI-made and were skipped.

Candidate 1, the Discover Scuba page's og:image: two first-time divers holding hands over a coral reef in clear blue water. 16:9 and sharp enough for a card, with slight JPEG softness. The site's Racha Yai trip gallery photos are only 850 px wide.

Hero of KBA's Phuket page, directly above its Rawai address: KBA's beach spot with orange KBA flags, a kite in the air and a student carrying a wing, with forested hills across the water. The hills rule out west-facing Nai Yang, so this is most likely the Rawai spot. Candidate 1 was a generic eFoil brand shot from the page's eFoil section, not Phuket. Sharp. The attention crop cuts the students at the bottom; position 'center' keeps the kite, the flags and the beach (checked).

From the same Phuket 101 article as the candidates: the white-and-gold chedi with naga railings, and Patong town and bay below. That is the hilltop view the card is about, while the two candidates show only the chedi (fisheye) and a naga statue. Commons has no photos of this temple. A small '©WillyThuan' mark sits bottom-left. The attention crop keeps it; position 'north' drops it and keeps the chedi and the bay (checked).

Candidate 1 (Phuket 101, Sept 2026): guests in rattan chairs on the cafe terrace at sunset, looking down the green valley to Patong Bay. Sharp. A small '© Phuket 101' mark sits bottom-right and falls outside the 16:9 attention crop (checked). The cafe's only official presence is a Facebook page.

Aerial drone shot of the Sail Away party boat at sea: the packed top deck with tables and dancers, the DJ booth at right, deep-blue water around. It comes from the gallery on the operator's own site. The 1235x925 PNG original has a 'SAIL AWAY' logo stamp near the bottom, so I saved only the top 16:9 band (1235x695, JPEG) and the logo is cut out. Rejected: candidate 1, the Megatix 800x800 Pukka Up promo (a close-up of a woman with both logos, probably Pukka Up's own Ibiza photo, not the Phuket boat). Also rejected: the two Megatix in-page collages, and the foam-party and DJ deck shots (logo stamps in the middle).

Fallback: the official DDT poster for 13 Jan 2027 at Lotus Arena Phuket (candidate 1, a text poster that is already 16:9: '13/01/2027 WED, DDT, LOTUS ARENA, PHUKET'). I found no real photo of Lotus Arena or Shaman. lotusarena.com has only flyers, ads and a logo; the Real Life Phuket article has only 3D renders from before the opening; Commons has nothing; no official Instagram or Facebook turned up. The other official flyers are also 16:9 (XOLIDAYBOY 23 Jan, media/191; Linda 17 Jan at Shaman, media/170; ICEGERGERT 24 Jan at Shaman, media/234). DDT is the headline concert, and its poster names the venue.

The hilltop pool terrace: a curved infinity pool with palms, rows of daybeds under navy-striped umbrellas, and the white club buildings with jungle behind. A sharp professional photo from the official gallery, already 16:9. I picked it over candidate 1 (the og:image, the same terrace but only 800x800 and square). Backup: an aerial of the busy club on the jungle hill (fira-beach-club-pool-trees.jpg, 1920x1080). The site's ocean-view photo has a dark overlay baked in.

Drone shot of the green-and-yellow Blanco party boat with a crowd on its top deck, by the limestone cliff at Viking Cave (bird's-nest scaffolding at left), in turquoise water. Already 16:9, with no logo. It is in Blanco's own WordPress media library (media ID 15283, Oct 2024, uploaded with the 'Koh Phi Phi's original boat party' logo). Its attachment link only redirects to the file, so page points to the boat party page; boat.jpg on Blanco's site shows the same boat. Rejected: candidate 1 (mayabayjump.jpg, only 624 px wide, a group jumping on Maya Bay beach rather than the boat). The boat party page's other images are tour-stop scenery.

The wooden pirate ship at sunset, anchored beside a limestone cliff, with guests on deck, flags in the rigging and a golden sky and sea. A professional photo used on the official site; I checked the pipeline's 16:9 attention crop and it keeps the ship and the cliff. Rejected: candidate 1 (a dark flash photo of the party crowd, faces close up) and candidate 2 (sunset from the deck, with a man's head filling the right half). Backup: nice-full-photo-phi-phi-pirate-boat.jpg (the ship in daylight, 2048x1536).

The night pool party at Ibiza: a crowd dancing and splashing in the pool under pink and yellow party lights, with the pool bar behind. The organiser's own photo from its pool party page. The 2048x1365 original has the 'IBIZA Pool Party' logo in the top right, so I saved the bottom 16:9 band (y 213-1365) and the logo is cut out. I skipped the Shutterstock and Unsplash images the site also uses. Rejected: candidate 1 (a daytime Commons view of Loh Dalum Bay, no party).

A night beach party on Loh Dalum Beach (Commons category 'Loh Dalum Beach', taken 26 Dec 2014 at 23:34): fire torches, a flaming limbo bar and a crowd of backpackers, which is the bar-strip scene. It is a phone photo, a bit soft and noisy but clear at card size. From the 1280px thumbnail I cut a 990x557 16:9 window on the left, so a crude hand-written bar sign on the right ('topless girls / naked boys free = bucket') is left out. This crop is a modification under CC BY-SA. Rejected: candidate 1 (a calm evening bay with no bars) and candidate 2 (a dim, blurry 2007 dusk beach). The Commons categories Loh Dalum Beach, Loh Dalum Bay, Ban Ton Sai and Ko Phi Phi Don have no other night or bar photo.

The tribute act live under purple light: two performers in Daft Punk-style helmets at the decks, one with an arm raised, above a huge open-air night crowd full of glowing lights. From the slideshow on the act's official site. It shows the act, not the Phangan venue: the venue is unclear (Jungle Experience on the ticket page, Ban Sabaii on phangan.events and Entrix). I chose a different photo from the Phuket Daft Funk card (which uses share.jpg), so the two cards don't look the same. Rejected: candidate 1 (the official square flyer, text-heavy with a QR code) and the 16:9 copy of the same flyer on lotusarena.com (media/220).

The sunset pool party itself: guests on the deck and in the infinity pool at golden hour, the pavilion bar on the left, and the sea and coast behind. This is candidate 2, the featured photo of the venue page: a 1280x578 phone panorama. The default attention crop cut out the pool and sea, so I saved the right-hand 16:9 window (x 252-1280, 1028x578). Backup: candidate 1 (2048x1365), a sharp shot of the empty deck with blue bean bags and a white lamp over the island view, but no party.

Sunset at Merkaba: palm silhouettes under pink clouds, guests at tables on the beach, the sea, and the lit blue pool in front. This is candidate 1 from the venue page (1280x960). The default attention crop kept only palms and sky, so I saved a centred 16:9 band (y 120-840, 1280x720). The venue pages' only other images are flyers, such as the Beach Bums 'The Coven' Halloween flyer.

credit: © YEP Listening Bar Koh Phangan (official YouTube channel @YEPLISTENINGBAR)
note: A party photo at YEP: the thumbnail of the venue's own video 'YEP & KOVËR CRËW' (YouTube oEmbed confirms the author is YEP LISTENING BAR KOH PHANGAN). It shows DJs at the Pioneer decks under red light, a hand fan, two people in balaclavas and the crowd, with the bar's red-brick wall behind. It is exactly 16:9. Rejected: the phangan.events candidate (IMG_7681) is a portrait close-up of the round YEP sign, which is close to a logo. The Facebook and Instagram og:images are the logo. The phangan.events and Telegram event images are text-heavy flyers. The phanganlife.com listing photos look Google-sourced (yep_01 is the same shot as a Google Places photo of YEP). The other channel thumbnails are the logo, a vertical frame or a man at a laptop.

Zen Beach at sunset (March 2025): people wading in the shallows and a paddleboarder under a sunset sky. Geotagged about 50 m from Grasshopper Beach Bar, which sits on Zen Beach per OpenStreetMap. Replaced the given candidate, which showed the main Sri Thanu beach (2008 photo), not Zen Beach. The 4:3 frame crops to 16:9 keeping the people and the sky.

The given candidate, kept: the Secret Party at night, a crowd in front of the red star-shaped stage under jungle trees. The organiser's small SECRET PARTY logo sits in the bottom-right corner and stays in the card crop (about 60 px wide on a phone). Every other image I found was a text flyer (26 phangan.events event posts, 4 megatix listings). secretpartykohtao.com and secretpartythailand.com are 'Coming Soon' pages.

license: venue photo via entrix.vip (the event's ticket page)
note: Night fire show at Hii Festival: a burning 'Hii KOH TAO' sign, a steel-wool fire spinner and sparks. Portrait, with the festival logo printed near the bottom (below y=1570). I ran the project's default 640x360 attention crop on it: it shows only the sign and sparks, no logo. If a crop is ever set by hand, keep it above the logo (BAND 560 works). Replaced the candidate, a soft portrait video frame of the hilltop Hii sign with a phangan.events caption. The official site hiifestivalkohtao.com has a good crowd photo, but its big logo sits in the middle of the crowd. The site's gallery is down because its Cloudinary account is disabled.

Drone shot at sunset of Sai Thong Beach, the festival's venue: palms, sand, rocks and sea. From the festival's own 'Sai Thong Beach - Koh Tao' gallery, with no watermark. Replaced the candidate, a text-heavy collage flyer. The festival's party photos all carry an 'lbmf' watermark (about 60 checked across 5 albums), so I chose this clean venue photo. It is square; the default crop keeps the palms and the beach. Warning: the festival homepage loads upload/1764142773.phtml and upload/album-1788851489.php as CSS backgrounds. These look like scripts planted on a hacked site; I did not open them. Be careful about linking leobeachmusicfestival.com in the guide.

Mae Haad pier seen from the sea on a clear day (14 Jan 2026): the 'Welcome to Koh Tao' gate, ferries and longtails tied up at the pier, the waterfront shops and the green hills behind. Sharp, 3:2, and the 16:9 crop keeps the pier and gate. Picked over the given 2014 night candidate (Hafen_Koh_TAO - panoramio), which shows the same gate but is dark.

The pier itself, from the official site of ONE°15 Marina Panwa Phuket, the marina at the same address (88/88 Moo 7 Wichit) that is taking over Visit Panwa Pier. It shows the old stilted pier building, the raised entrance deck with the white house-shaped frames (as in phuketferry's 422 px entrance photo and Love Andaman's crew photo on this pier), the green channel and the tip of the new pontoon. Saved as a 16:9 crop (x 848, y 0, 1200x675) of the 2048x2048 original, with no people in frame; the attention crop of the square original would pick the tool-strewn deck with three workers, so do not re-crop it. Rejected: ONE°15's cover and site hero (CGI rendering of the 2027 marina), its other photos (barge, fuel tanks, cafe, logo), Love Andaman's crew portrait and lounge shots, its fleet photo (text graphic, place unconfirmed), Sail Away party shots, stock images on Openferry and Bookaway. Commons (5 km geosearch, Thai names), Openverse and a Flickr CC geosearch found nothing of the pier.

The venue's own flyer for 'Sedo Izikura featuring Alam B2B Jah' (21 Jan 2025, RA): a black-and-white photo of two DJs on the decks, with the title at the top and 'SÉDO IZIKURA, Japanese home cooking & underground music' at the bottom. The default attention crop keeps the hands on the decks and the venue name, cuts the faces and drops the old date. BAND 250 instead shows both faces and the decks with no text. No real venue photo could be found: all 21 phangan.events listings are flyers, the RA venue page has no photo, Instagram blocks access and there is no website. Both given candidates are text-heavy portrait flyers whose 16:9 crop is mostly title text or a past date (17.10.26).

The given candidate: the venue's Tree Secret jungle-techno flyer (Fri 16 Oct 2026), with resident DJ Annabelle at the decks in a lit jungle. Portrait, but the 16:9 attention crop keeps her face, 'Jungle Techno' and the 'Resident DJ Annabelle' sign, and drops the date and address text. A flyer was used because no real venue or party photo exists in the sources I could reach: all 41 phangan.events listings are flyers; RA's 'Sound Garden Tattoo Club' page (79/24 M.1 Thong Sala) has no photo, only 2019-2024 flyers; the Tattoo Club Facebook cover is a logo and its reel thumbnails are only 540 px wide.
Sunset with palm trees at Promthep Cape (Commons, from Flickr, 31 Mar 2017). License checked on Commons, 20 Oct 2026; checked by eye.
